body.statement: Does \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}<\rho_n^W\) hold for every even \(n\ge10\)? Derive either a legal all-size family of full-count perturbations and matching active-state inequalities, or an explicit later even counterexample with a scalar saddle certificate. The derivation must control every new response-type state and cannot infer persistence from the \(n=8\) witness alone.
body.justification: Strictness need not propagate because padding changes allocation mixtures, the feasible state lattice, and least-favorable supports.
body.gap: Hull states a related general complete-randomization conjecture, while no located source gives the required uniform separating-prior or active-gradient argument for this compression comparison.
body.consumer: A resolution would determine whether software should preserve the second count at every larger balanced binary experiment or only at selected sizes.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform proof of strict full-count improvement for every later positive even population size, or a certified later counterexample, remains open.
obligation.obstruction: The eight-unit separating rule does not embed into a later balanced experiment: padding changes the treated allocation mixture and introduces new response-type states whose risks are uncontrolled by the finite certificate.
obligation.attempted: The exact eight-unit witness and the general information inequality were checked, but neither supplies a legal all-size perturbation or a least-favorable scalar support characterization.
obligation.partial_result: The finite calculation proves \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}<\rho_8^W\), while Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}response\mbox{-}type\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}games}\) proves only the weak inequality \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq\rho_n^W\) at every positive even \(n\).  No implication from the strict inequality at eight to any even \(n\geq10\) has been established.
